scope_guard: Random topology matching U10 cardinalities, not the exact U10 graph, not Hostinger/Andreas target evidence, and not a universal database benchmark.

prepared_index_memory_shadow.measurement_guard: sys.getsizeof recursive approximation; Python allocator/RSS and production representation will differ materially. Use only as a local memory-amplification warning.

negative_result: V1 full prepared-ref materialization is NOT_SELECTED for the affected-anchor hot path because on-demand BFS is materially faster on this fixture.
candidate_result: V2 anchor-mask intersection preserves the same affected-anchor set and is materially faster than both V1 materialization and BFS on this fixture, but consumes a much larger prepared support structure than BFS.

architecture_adjudication.selection_law: choose from measured read/update/memory/recompile break-even; no unconditional default

strongest_counterhypothesis: On real ClayGraph topology the support index may amplify memory/cache misses and update cost enough that a 2-hop BFS, compressed bitmap, or specialized dynamic graph representation dominates end-to-end.
next_falsifiers: Replay exact U10 topology and real mutation trace.
Measure process RSS/cache behavior and support-pair growth on hub/pathological graphs.
Measure full U10 weighted-field recompile time saved per mutation, not only invalidation lookup.
Compare dense Python-int masks with Roaring/sorted sparse anchor sets and on-demand BFS.
Run Hostinger Ubuntu and final Andreas Ubuntu target measurements.
